title: Full Walkthrough: Workflow for AI Coding — Matt Pocock
talk_summary: Matt Pocock demonstrates a human-in-loop planning workflow: grill for shared understanding, write a PRD, split into vertical-slice Kanban issues, then let AFK agents implement with TDD and fresh-context review. He emphasizes context smart zones, feedback loops, deep modules, and parallel sandboxed worktrees.

takeaways.technique: Clear context instead of compacting; enforce smart-zone budget
takeaways.what_they_do: Tracks token usage and treats roughly 100K tokens as the smart-zone marker, preferring a hard context reset over compacting history that accumulates sediment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I much prefer my AI to behave like uh the guy from Memento because this state is always the same.
takeaways.numbers: ~100K token smart-zone marker; 1M context window still has a dumb zone

takeaways.what_they_do: A tiny skill interviews relentlessly, one question at a time with recommended answers, until the human and model reach a shared design concept before planning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Interview me relentlessly about every aspect of this plan until we reach a shared understanding.

takeaways.technique: Vertical-slice Kanban DAG, not sequential phases
takeaways.evidence_quote: break a PRD into independently grabbable issues using vertical slices traceable bullets
takeaways.numbers: example PRD had 18 user stories and 5 issues

takeaways.technique: TDD red-green-refactor to prevent test cheating
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent writes a failing test first, confirms red, implements to green, then runs tests/types; TDD instruments code before implementation so the model is less likely to write tests after the fact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: TDD I found is absolutely essential for getting the most out of agents.
takeaways.numbers: 284 tests in repo after run; one type error fixed

takeaways.technique: Fresh-context review with pushed standards and stronger reviewer
takeaways.what_they_do: After implementation, clears context and runs review in the smart zone; pushes coding standards to the reviewer while letting implementers pull skills as needed, and uses a stronger model for review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you clear the context, then you're essentially going to be able to just review in the smart zone

takeaways.technique: Parallel worktrees in Docker with merger agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Planner selects parallel issues, creates a sandbox/worktree per issue, runs implementers, reviews commits, then a merger agent merges branches and fixes type/test conflicts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for each issue, we create a sandbox and then we run an implementer in that sandbox
